title: NFTStakerDepletion.depositFor settles a staker's pending phUSD with _safePay, paying the MIGRATOR while emitting Claimed(user, …)
description: `_safePay` forwards to `_safePayTo(msg.sender, …)`, and `depositFor` is `onlyMigrator`, so msg.sender is ALWAYS an orchestrator contract and never the user. The contract already defines and correctly uses `_safePayTo` in `_exitPosition` (:733) — this is a missed call-site, not a missing primitive. story-021 wrote the fix into the new fourth copy (NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:887), named the defect in its own commit body ('which would pay the migrator'), called it 'wrong in every case' in the ported NatSpec, and then explicitly left NFTStakerDepletion.sol untouched.
impact: A migrated user's fully-accrued (matured) phUSD reward is transferred to the migrator contract instead of the user. On the InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator path it is recoverable by owner rescueERC20 (manual hand-distribution). On the NFTStakerMigrator path it is PERMANENTLY LOST — that contract has no rescueERC20, no rescueERC1155, no fallback and no receive (DEDUP-20-010). PoC testD confirms 82,191.78 phUSD permanently stranded.
attackPath: 1. No attacker is required. This is the ordinary, intended operational path.
2. Operator initiates a cross-staker migration whose orchestrator is NFTStakerMigrator.

4. depositFor settles the user's pending reward via _safePay, which forwards to _safePayTo(msg.sender, …). Because depositFor is onlyMigrator, msg.sender is ALWAYS the orchestrator and NEVER the user.
5. The full pending balance lands on NFTStakerMigrator; Claimed(user, amount) is emitted anyway, so off-chain reconciliation reports the user was paid.
6. NFTStakerMigrator exposes no recovery function of any kind. The phUSD is unrecoverable by anyone, including the owner.
likelihood: high on the affected path — deterministic, not probabilistic. Every migrated user who already held a position on the target pool loses their entire accrued balance on that call. Mitigating timing fact: neither migrator is deployed today, so present on-chain exposure is zero.
assumptions: The user being migrated already holds a position on the target pool (otherwise pending == 0 and nothing is misrouted). The migration is run through NFTStakerMigrator rather than InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.
externalRequirements: None beyond the operator running the documented migration. No attacker, no market conditions, no privileged misuse.
justification: C4 High: 'assets can be stolen/LOST/compromised'. Loss counts, and this is loss of MATURED yield, which project law treats as equivalent to capital loss (unmatured/in-motion yield is what caps at Medium; this is settled, pending, owed). There are no hand-wavy hypotheticals: the path is the intended one, the PoC is 4/4 PASS with a genuine control (testB proves batchMigrate pays correctly, so the defect is path-specific rather than a blanket claim), and the loss is terminal because the receiving contract has no recovery primitive whatsoever. The defect is a known-and-named bug: story-021's own commit body identifies '_safePay … which would pay the migrator', its ported NatSpec calls the _safePay form 'wrong in every case', and the fix was written into the new fourth copy (NFTStakerPriceScaledMigrateReady.sol:887) while NFTStakerDepletion.sol was explicitly left untouched.
recommendation: The primitive already exists and is already used correctly at _exitPosition (:733). The fix is a single call-site change to _safePayTo(user, …). Per WATCH-17 (now 4-way, D-05) verify the same call site in ALL FOUR staker copies before closing.

disputeFlag.dispute: Medium vs plausible High. Filed HIGH per D-10 (file higher, record the dispute) and the matured-yield rule.
disputeFlag.counterReadingPreservedVerbatim: OPEN — requires severity-auditor arbitration. Plausible HIGH for the NFTStakerMigrator orchestrator (user funds permanently lost, no recovery path of any kind). Filed Medium because (a) no attacker is required or benefits, (b) magnitude is bounded by pending accrued on the TARGET pool for users already holding a position there, (c) the solvency invariant is not broken, (d) neither migrator is deployed.
disputeFlag.conditionUnderWhichMediumIsCorrect: If the operator confirms NFTStakerMigrator is dead code that will never be deployed, and every future migration will run through InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator (which HAS rescueERC20), the loss becomes recoverable-with-manual-effort and Medium is the honest label. That confirmation has not been given, and the contract is live in the repo and in scope.

whyNotMedium: The four grounds offered for Medium do not survive weighing. (a) 'No attacker required or benefits' is not a mitigant for a loss finding — it removes the adversarial precondition and therefore RAISES likelihood to deterministic. (b) 'Magnitude bounded by pending accrued' is a bound, not a smallness claim: the PoC measures 82,191.78 phUSD, which is not dust. (c) 'Solvency invariant not broken' means the protocol stays solvent while individual users are made whole-less — protocol solvency is not the asset at issue. (d) 'Neither migrator is deployed' bounds PRESENT EXPOSURE, not the severity of the code as written, and pre-deployment is precisely when a self-audit has leverage.

orchestratorRuling.verdict: HIGH CONFIRMED, with the loss population tightened.
orchestratorRuling.scopeTightening: The `if (info.amount > 0)` guard at NFTStakerDepletion.sol:753 means ONLY a user who already holds a non-zero position ON THE TARGET staker loses anything. On a migration into a freshly-deployed target every user has pending == 0 and nothing is misrouted. The realistic loss population is users holding stake in BOTH pools — which permissionless stake() on the target makes ordinary, not exotic.
orchestratorRuling.magnitudeHonesty: The PoC's 82,191.78 phUSD is a LAB magnitude produced by the test fixture. It is NOT a predicted mainnet loss and must not be reported as one.
orchestratorRuling.whyHighStands: 'Not deployed' is a DEPLOYMENT-STATUS fact, not a severity bound — discounting for non-deployment would make every pre-deployment self-audit finding Low, inverting the point of auditing before deployment. And NFTStakerMigrator's own NatSpec (:9-11) names NFTStakerDepletion as its documented target type: 'Orchestrates a zero-user-action migration between two NFTStakerDepletion instances.' The buggy contract is the documented target of the no-rescue migrator.
orchestratorRuling.conditionUnderWhichMediumBecomesCorrect: An operator statement that NFTStakerMigrator will never be deployed and every migration runs through InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator (which HAS rescueERC20). Not given.
orchestratorRuling.riderIfDowngraded: If a human downgrades this to Medium, L-02 (CLASS-013, NFTStakerMigrator has no rescue) becomes the SOLE carrier of the permanence fact and MUST be re-weighed at that time — not left at Low by inertia (severity-auditor §4).
